Overview

Fabrikam Lettings Ltd's Microsoft 365 tenant was reviewed on 19/10/2026 against 131 checks across 15 areas. The weighted score is 44% (Red). Of the checks assessed, 20 failed, 77 need attention and 15 passed. 16 high-severity issues should be addressed first. Estimated remediation effort for all failed and warning items is about 357.0 hours (47.6 days).

The tenant already has licences for features that are not being used. Not used: 7. Partly used: 11. Setting these up is estimated at 36.5 days (see Opportunities).

Against the published benchmarks the tenant meets: CIS v7.0.0 22% (29 of 130 assessed controls, 15 to check manually); CISA SCuBA 26% (24 of 92 assessed controls, 6 to check manually) (see Benchmarks).

Azure was reviewed separately (2 subscriptions): the Azure score is 26%, with 9 failed and 18 needing attention (see Azure).

Servers were reviewed separately (6 systems from collected server data): the server score is 10%, with 21 failed and 7 needing attention (see Servers).

1Must do: start within 2 weeks

Serious gaps that leave the business open to attack, data loss or disruption today. These should be fixed first.

Patch, protect and back up servers

About 5.5 days

Why it matters. Servers hold your most important data and systems. Servers that are out of support, unpatched, unprotected or not backed up are the most common way ransomware gets in and causes lasting damage.

  • Windows servers run a supported version2.5 daysWe found: 1 of 5 Windows servers is out of support; 1 more loses support within six months.
  • Windows servers are patched and rebooted4 hoursWe found: 1 of 5 servers is missing security updates.
  • Windows servers have working EDR and antivirus2 hoursWe found: 1 of 5 servers has no EDR.
  • Remote management is not exposed or weakly protected2 hoursWe found: 1 of 5 servers allows weakly protected remote access.
  • SMBv1 is disabled and SMB signing is required2 hoursWe found: SMBv1 is enabled on 1 server; signing is not required on 2 servers.
  • Local administrator accounts are managed3 hoursWe found: 1 of 3 member servers has unmanaged local administrator accounts.
  • Servers are backed up2 hoursWe found: 1 server has not completed a Windows Server Backup in the last two days.
  • No out-of-support server software1.5 daysWe found: 4 items of out-of-support software were found.
What your staff will noticeServers may need short, planned restarts outside working hours.
What we need from youAgree a maintenance window, and budget for replacing any servers that are out of support.

Secure Active Directory

About 2.5 days

Why it matters. Active Directory controls sign-in to every PC and server. A weakness here can let one compromised account take over the whole network.

  • Active Directory replication and SYSVOL are healthy4 hoursWe found: 2 replication or SYSVOL problems found.
  • Privileged AD groups are small and protected3 hoursWe found: Domain Admins is too large (7 members; two to four is recommended).
  • No accounts open to Kerberos and delegation attacks4 hoursWe found: 2 high-risk account settings found (3 more to review).
  • Domain password and lockout policy is strong2 hoursWe found: The domain password or lockout policy is weak: minimum length 8, no account lockout, history 12.
  • Domain controllers are hardened3 hoursWe found: Both domain controllers need hardening.
What your staff will noticeMostly no change. A few old accounts may be disabled and some service accounts given new passwords.
What we need from youConfirm which old accounts and service accounts are still needed.

Secure your Azure services

About 2.5 days

Why it matters. Cloud servers and services that are open to the internet, or have no security monitoring, are a frequent target for attackers.

  • Microsoft Defender for Cloud protects servers and data services3 hoursWe found: 3 Defender plans are not on for resources in use, including Defender for Servers in 1 subscription. The plans in Fabrikam Dev could not be read (the account needs Security Reader or Reader there).
  • Management ports are not open to the internet2 hoursWe found: 1 rule in use allows management or database ports from the internet.
  • Servers run a supported operating system1.5 daysWe found: 3 servers are out of support. 1 more server is on extended security updates or loses support within six months.
  • Azure servers are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint3 hoursWe found: 2 of 3 running servers are not onboarded to Defender for Endpoint.
  • Storage accounts block public access and require TLS 1.22 hoursWe found: 1 of 2 storage accounts allows anonymous access, HTTP or old TLS.
What your staff will noticeNo change for staff.
What we need from youConfirm which Azure services must be reachable from the internet.

Protect sign-ins and accounts

About 1.5 days

Why it matters. Most attacks start with a stolen or guessed password. These changes make it much harder for anyone to get into a staff account, even if they have the password.

  • Licensed users are registered for MFA4 hoursWe found: 88% of 25 enabled licensed users are MFA capable (3 not capable).
  • All administrators are registered for MFA1 hourWe found: Admin accounts not MFA capable: 1 of 7.
  • Users cannot consent to applications1 hourWe found: Users can consent to any application for any delegated permission.
  • Directory synchronisation is healthy2 hoursWe found: Last sync 18/10/2026 03:50 (30 hours ago).
What your staff will noticeStaff may be asked to set up an authenticator app and could be prompted to sign in again on their devices.
What we need from youAgree a date to tell staff, and confirm any shared or emergency accounts that need different treatment.

  • Security logging and audit policy are in place2 hours
  • Unnecessary and risky services are not running2 hours
  • Physical servers encrypt their disks2 hours
What your staff will noticeServers may need short, planned restarts outside working hours.
What we need from youAgree a maintenance window, and budget for replacing any servers that are out of support.

Secure Active Directory

About 3 hours

Why it matters. Active Directory controls sign-in to every PC and server. A weakness here can let one compromised account take over the whole network.

  • Stale and out-of-support accounts are cleaned up3 hours
What your staff will noticeMostly no change. A few old accounts may be disabled and some service accounts given new passwords.
What we need from youConfirm which old accounts and service accounts are still needed.

Keep virtualisation hosts healthy

About 1.5 days

Why it matters. One host runs many servers, so a problem there affects all of them. Old snapshots, unsupported versions and missing redundancy put every virtual server at risk.

  • Hyper-V hosts are dedicated1.5 days
What your staff will noticeHosts may need planned maintenance windows.
What we need from youAgree maintenance windows and any budget for host upgrades.

Patch and harden Linux servers

About 1 hour

Why it matters. Linux servers often run websites, databases and file transfers that face the internet. Keeping them patched and locked down stops them becoming a way in.

  • Linux disk space, packages and kernel settings1 hour
What your staff will noticeServers may need short, planned restarts outside working hours.
What we need from youAgree a maintenance window and who owns each server.

Secure your Azure services

About 4 days

Why it matters. Cloud servers and services that are open to the internet, or have no security monitoring, are a frequent target for attackers.

  • Defender for Cloud secure score1.5 days
  • Microsoft cloud security benchmark compliance1.5 days
  • Virtual machines do not have public IP addresses2 hours
  • Subnets are protected by network security groups2 hours
  • Key vaults have purge protection and restricted network access1 hour
  • Servers have no outstanding critical or security updates3 hours
  • Defender for Cloud alert emails reach the right people30 minutes
  • Virtual machines use Trusted Launch2 hours
What your staff will noticeNo change for staff.
What we need from youConfirm which Azure services must be reachable from the internet.

Make sure Azure can recover

About 6 hours

Why it matters. Backups and protection against accidental deletion mean a mistake or a ransomware attack does not become a lasting outage.

  • Backup vaults are protected against deletion and ransomware1 hour
  • High-impact Azure Advisor recommendations4 hours
  • Azure Arc servers are connected1 hour
What your staff will noticeNo change for staff.
What we need from youConfirm how much data you could afford to lose and how quickly systems must be back.

Control Azure access and cost

About 7 hours

Why it matters. Clear ownership, budgets and removing unused resources stop surprise bills and limit who can change live systems.

  • The Azure activity log is kept beyond 90 days1 hour
  • Critical resources have delete locks1 hour
  • No unattached disks or unused public IP addresses1 hour
  • Azure Advisor cost recommendations2 hours
  • Every subscription has a budget alert30 minutes
  • The Microsoft cloud security benchmark policy is assigned1 hour
  • Network Watcher is enabled where networks exist30 minutes
What your staff will noticeNo change for staff.
What we need from youAgree a monthly Azure budget and who should be alerted.

4. Prioritised recommendations

This is the technical list for engineers; the Action plan gives the same work in plain English. Priority P1 items (must do) are high-severity failures to fix first, P2 (should do) are medium-severity failures or high-severity warnings, and P3 (could do) are improvements and manual checks. Effort is an estimate of engineer hours for remediation and is for scoping only. Total: 357.0 hours (47.6 days at 7.5 hours per day).

PriorityRecommendationAreaStatusEffort (hours)
P1Active Directory replication and SYSVOL are healthy AD-01
Fix replication errors (repadmin /showrepl, dcdiag) so every domain controller has replicated in the last day, and migrate SYSVOL from FRS to DFS Replication if it has not been done.		Active DirectoryFail4
P1Privileged AD groups are small and protected AD-02
Keep Domain Admins to two to four named admin accounts (separate from day-to-day accounts), leave Enterprise Admins and Schema Admins empty until needed, empty Account, Server, Print and Backup Operators, and add admin accounts to Protected Users.		Active DirectoryFail3
P1No accounts open to Kerberos and delegation attacks AD-03
Remove service principal names from admin accounts and use group managed service accounts with long random passwords for services, turn Kerberos pre-authentication back on, clear "password not required" and reversible encryption flags, remove unconstrained delegation from non-DC computers and users, and remove passwords from account descriptions.		Active DirectoryFail4
P1Domain password and lockout policy is strong AD-04
Set the default domain password policy to a minimum of 14 characters with complexity, keep 24 passwords of history, lock accounts after 5 to 10 failed attempts for at least 15 minutes, and never allow reversible encryption. Use fine-grained policies for admins and service accounts.		Active DirectoryFail2
P1Domain controllers are hardened AD-07
On every domain controller require LDAP signing (LDAPServerIntegrity 2) and enforce LDAP channel binding, disable the Print Spooler, run a supported Windows Server version, and do not install other roles or software on DCs.		Active DirectoryFail3
P1Microsoft Defender for Cloud protects servers and data services AZ-02
Turn on Defender for Servers (Plan 1 at least, which includes Defender for Endpoint) in every subscription with virtual machines or Arc servers, and Defender for Storage, SQL and Key Vault where those resources hold client data. (MCSB LT-1, ES-1)		Azure securityFail3
P1Management ports are not open to the internet AZ-06
Remove network security group rules that allow RDP, SSH, WinRM, SMB or database ports from Any or Internet. Use Azure Bastion, Defender for Cloud just-in-time access or a VPN for administration, and limit any remaining rules to known source addresses. (MCSB NS-1, NS-2)		Azure securityFail2
P1No retired Basic SKU public IPs or load balancers AZ-09
Upgrade Basic SKU public IP addresses and Basic load balancers to Standard. Microsoft retired both on 30 September 2025, so Basic resources are no longer supported and can stop working.		Azure resilienceFail4
P1Virtual machines are backed up AZ-10
Protect every virtual machine with Azure Backup (or confirm another backup product covers it), with daily backups, at least 30 days of retention and alerts on failed jobs. Investigate any backup that has not completed in the last two days. (MCSB BR-1, BR-3)		Azure resilienceFail3
P1Servers run a supported operating system AZ-12
Upgrade or replace servers whose operating system is out of support (Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 extended security updates ended on 13 October 2026; Windows Server 2016 support ends on 12 January 2027). Plan upgrades for anything ending within six months. (MCSB PV-6)		Azure securityFail8
P1Azure servers are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint AZ-13
Onboard every running server to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (Defender for Servers deploys the MDE extension automatically). Replace the retired Log Analytics agent (MMA/OMS) with the Azure Monitor agent where monitoring data is needed. (MCSB ES-1, LT-1)		Azure securityFail3
P1Storage accounts block public access and require TLS 1.2 AZ-15
On every storage account, turn off anonymous blob access, require secure transfer with TLS 1.2 or later, restrict network access to selected networks or private endpoints, and disable shared key access where applications support Entra ID authentication. (MCSB NS-2, DP-3, IM-1)		Azure securityFail2
P1Subscription owners are limited and not guests AZ-19
Keep subscription Owner and User Access Administrator to two or three named admins through groups, make them eligible through Privileged Identity Management rather than permanent, remove guests and unused service principals, and review the CSP partner access. (MCSB PA-1, PA-7)		Azure governance and costFail2
P1Devices are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint DEF-01
Onboard every Windows and macOS device to Defender for Endpoint or Defender for Business, ideally with the Intune EDR onboarding policy, and confirm each device reports in the Defender portal.		Microsoft Defender XDRFail4
P1No critical vulnerabilities with public exploits DEF-04
Patch the listed software through the RMM or Intune, starting with critical vulnerabilities that have public exploits. Remove software that is no longer needed and make sure third-party applications are in the patch policy.		Microsoft Defender XDRFail8
P1Security incidents are triaged and resolved DEF-08
Assign, investigate and resolve open incidents, starting with high severity. Make sure incident notifications reach your service desk or SOC.		Microsoft Defender XDRFail2
P1SPF records are valid DNS-01
Publish exactly one SPF record per domain that includes spf.protection.outlook.com and every other legitimate sender, ending in -all or ~all.		Email authenticationFail1
P1DKIM signing is enabled for every mail domain DNS-02
Publish the selector1 and selector2 CNAME records and enable DKIM signing in Defender for each custom domain.		Email authenticationFail1
P1DMARC is published and enforced DNS-03
Publish DMARC for every domain, start at p=none with reporting, then move to p=quarantine and p=reject once legitimate senders pass SPF or DKIM.		Email authenticationFail1
P1Compliance policies cover every enrolled platform END-01
Create and assign a compliance policy for each platform in use (Windows, iOS/iPadOS, Android, macOS) covering encryption, OS version, password and Defender status.		Intune and devicesFail4
P1Windows devices are encrypted END-05
Deploy a BitLocker disk encryption policy from Endpoint security and escrow recovery keys to Entra ID.		Intune and devicesFail4
P1Windows devices run a supported version END-06
Upgrade Windows 10 devices (out of support since 14 October 2025 unless covered by ESU) and Windows 11 builds below the minimum to a supported release.		Intune and devicesFail4
P1Apple MDM push certificate is valid END-13
Renew the Apple MDM push certificate in Intune (Devices, Enrolment, Apple) before it expires, using the same Apple ID that created it. Use a shared company Apple ID, not a personal one. If it expires, Apple devices stop receiving policy, and creating a new certificate with a different Apple ID means re-enrolling every Apple device.		Intune connectionsFail1
P1Mailbox forwarding is reviewed EXO-06
Confirm every mailbox forward is authorised, particularly to external addresses. Unexpected forwarding is a common sign of a compromised account.		Exchange OnlineFail1
P1Licensed users are registered for MFA IAM-05
Run an MFA registration campaign and follow up with users who are not registered. Unregistered accounts can be registered by an attacker who has the password.		Identity and accessFail4
P1All administrators are registered for MFA IAM-06
Register strong MFA methods for every account that holds an admin role before anything else. Remove roles from accounts that do not need them.		Identity and accessFail1
P1Users cannot consent to applications IAM-13
Set user consent to "Do not allow" or "Allow for verified publishers, for selected low-impact permissions", and turn on the admin consent workflow.		Identity and accessFail1
P1Directory synchronisation is healthy IAM-22
Investigate the Entra Connect or Cloud Sync server. A stalled sync means leavers disabled on-premises keep cloud access.		Identity and accessFail2
P1Linux servers run a supported release and are patched LNX-01
Upgrade servers on releases that no longer receive security updates (or add extended support such as Ubuntu Pro), install outstanding security updates, restart servers that need it, and turn on automatic security updates where the workload allows.		Linux serversFail8
P1Linux SSH and accounts are hardened LNX-02
In sshd_config set PermitRootLogin no, PasswordAuthentication no (keys only), PermitEmptyPasswords no and MaxAuthTries 4 or lower. Remove extra UID 0 accounts and empty passwords, and limit passwordless sudo to specific commands.		Linux serversFail2
P1Linux servers have EDR, a firewall and audit logging LNX-03
Install Defender for Endpoint on Linux (or the client's EDR), turn on the host firewall (ufw or firewalld) with a default-deny inbound policy, keep SELinux enforcing or AppArmor enabled, run auditd, and make sure time is synchronised.		Linux serversFail3
P1No guest accounts hold admin roles PRV-02
Remove admin roles from guest accounts. Partner access should use GDAP, not guest accounts with roles.		Privileged accessFail0.5
P1Windows servers run a supported version SRV-01
Upgrade or replace servers whose Windows Server version is out of support (2012 and 2012 R2 extended security updates ended on 13 October 2026; Windows Server 2016 support ends on 12 January 2027). Plan upgrades for anything ending within six months.		Windows serversFail16
P1Windows servers are patched and rebooted SRV-02
Install the outstanding security updates and restart servers that are waiting for a reboot. Check the RMM patch policy covers every server and that servers are restarted at least monthly.		Windows serversFail4
P1Windows servers have working EDR and antivirus SRV-03
Onboard every server to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (Defender for Servers or Defender for Business servers) or the client's chosen EDR, keep real-time protection and tamper protection on, and make sure signatures update daily.		Windows serversFail2
P1Remote management is not exposed or weakly protected SRV-04
Require Network Level Authentication for Remote Desktop, limit RDP, SMB and WinRM firewall rules to management subnets instead of any address, and turn off unencrypted and Basic authentication on WinRM.		Windows serversFail2
P1SMBv1 is disabled and SMB signing is required SRV-05
Remove the SMB 1.0 feature, and require SMB signing on servers (Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)) through Group Policy, after checking for old devices such as copiers that still need SMBv1.		Windows serversFail2
P1Local administrator accounts are managed SRV-07
Deploy Windows LAPS to every member server so the local administrator password is unique and rotated, disable the Guest account, and remove broad groups such as Domain Users or Everyone from the local Administrators group.		Windows serversFail3
P1Servers are backed up SRV-10
Confirm every server is covered by a backup with offsite or immutable copies: physical servers need a backup agent, and virtual machines need either an agent or host-level backup. Test a restore at least quarterly.		Windows serversFail2
P1No out-of-support server software SRV-12
Plan upgrades or migrations for software that no longer receives security updates, such as SQL Server 2016 and older, Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 (move to Exchange Online or Exchange Server Subscription Edition), and old Java, PHP or .NET runtimes.		Windows serversFail8
P2LAPS covers domain computers AD-08
Extend the schema for Windows LAPS (Update-LapsADSchema), grant computers permission to update their password (Set-LapsADComputerSelfPermission) and deploy a LAPS policy to every workstation and member server OU.		Active DirectoryWarning3
P2High-risk application permissions are reviewed APP-01
Review each non-Microsoft application holding high-impact application permissions (mail, files, directory write). Remove apps that are unused or unknown and reduce permissions where possible.		ApplicationsWarning3
P2Windows LAPS policy manages local administrator passwords END-19
In Endpoint security, Account protection, create a Local admin password solution (Windows LAPS) policy that backs up the password to Microsoft Entra ID, rotates it at least every 30 days and after use, and assign it to all Windows devices. Microsoft Entra LAPS must also be enabled in Entra device settings (IAM-25).		Windows security configurationWarning2
P2BitLocker policy requires encryption and escrows recovery keys END-20
In Endpoint security, Disk encryption, create a BitLocker policy that requires device encryption, uses silent encryption, and saves operating system drive recovery information to Microsoft Entra ID before encrypting. Assign it to all Windows devices.		Windows security configurationWarning3
P2Attack surface reduction rules are in block mode END-22
Deploy the attack surface reduction rules from Endpoint security, Attack surface reduction. Put the three standard protection rules (vulnerable signed drivers, credential stealing from LSASS, persistence through WMI) into block mode straight away, run the others in audit mode for two to four weeks, review the audit events in Defender, then switch them to block.		Windows security configurationWarning4
P2Legacy authentication is blocked IAM-02
Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks Exchange ActiveSync and other legacy clients for all users. Check sign-in logs for legacy clients first, then enforce.		Identity and accessWarning2
P2Directory recovery and krbtgt hygiene AD-05
Turn on the AD Recycle Bin, reset the krbtgt password (twice, at least 10 hours apart) if it has not changed in 180 days, set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 so ordinary users cannot join computers, and raise the domain and forest functional levels to Windows Server 2016.		Active DirectoryFail2
P2App Service apps enforce HTTPS and TLS 1.2 AZ-18

P2Windows Firewall is enforced on every profile END-21

P2Between two and four Global Administrators PRV-01

9. Inventory

10. Method and limitations

Data was collected read-only through Microsoft Graph (including Defender XDR advanced hunting for the last 30 days), the Exchange Online management API and the Security & Compliance management API, plus the Teams, SharePoint, Fabric and Power Platform admin APIs where access was approved, using delegated access by engineer@reviewer.example. No settings were changed. DNS records were checked from public DNS. Each check compares the current configuration with Microsoft guidance and Contoso IT standards.

Azure was read through Azure Resource Manager, Azure Resource Graph, Defender for Cloud and Azure Advisor with the Azure roles of engineer@reviewer.example, after read access was approved at the start of the review. Only subscriptions where that account has a role are included (2 subscriptions).

Server data was collected separately with the Contoso IT server collectors (run on each Windows server as an administrator, through the RMM or over WinRM; a shell script on Linux; PowerCLI for VMware) and imported from 8 data files. Each server is compared with CIS Level 1 and Microsoft security baseline settings, supported versions, patching, protection and backup.

Licence utilisation compares the service plans in each user's assigned licences (excluding plans switched off on the licence) with configuration and 30-day usage reports. A feature shown as Not used is licensed but has no matching configuration or activity. Usage reports can lag by up to 48 hours.

169 of 180 collection steps succeeded. 0 failed and 11 were unavailable or skipped (often because a feature is not licensed). Checks that depend on missing data are shown as Not assessed. The Collection diagnostics inventory lists every step.

Not covered by automated checks

  • Backup of Microsoft 365 data
  • File and folder level permissions inside SharePoint sites and OneDrive (site membership is covered through groups and Teams)
  • Defender for Cloud Apps policies and Defender portal advanced settings (licence use is flagged in Opportunities)
  • Purview communication compliance, information barriers and records management file plans

Areas reviewed

Identity and access, Applications and consents, Licensing, Exchange Online and email security, Email DNS (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams, Intune and devices, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Secure Score, Licence utilisation opportunities, CIS v7 and CISA SCuBA benchmarks, Teams, SharePoint, Power BI and Power Platform settings, Mailbox permissions, Group, Team and site membership, Azure subscriptions and resources, Servers (imported server data)

Effort estimates assume the remediation is carried out by an experienced engineer with suitable admin access and exclude user communication, change control and testing with the client unless stated.
